dct_description_sm: The North of the province of Qubec is populated by communities for whom drinking water mainly comes from surface water sources. Although rivers and lakes are abundant in this region, they are of variable quality, vulnerable to contamination and unreliable because they freeze or run dry quickly during winter. However, the groundwater contained in aquifers has better quality and usually requires minimal treatment due to the large filtering capacity of soils. The dynamics of groundwater in northern areas is directly related to the presence of permafrost. However, permafrost is currently degrading due to temperature increases related to climate changes. Permafrost degradation can increase access to groundwater as a source for drinking water. In this context, the main objective of the project is to produce a water balance in a small watershed located close to Umiujaq where there is discontinuous permafrost
dct_title_s: Water balance data in Umiujaq, Nunavik, Qubec
